mainTopic: Rules for the מתורגמן and skipping in the reading, and why the מפטיר leads the prayers
overview: This amud finishes the משנה's rules for reading with a מתורגמן. In נביא the reader may give three verses at a time, unless each verse is its own paragraph. Skipping is allowed in נביא but not in the Torah. The גמרא explains that the three-verse minimum for each Torah reader matches תורה, נביאים, and כתובים (רב אסי), and it gives ישעיה 52:3-5 as an example of verses that are separate paragraphs. A contradiction from the כהן גדול's יום כיפור reading leads אביי to rule that in the Torah one may skip within one topic, and a ברייתא confirms this. A second ברייתא forbids skipping from one book of נביא to another, though skipping forward within תרי עשר is allowed. A new משנה then gives the מפטיר the honor of leading the prayers and lists what a קטן, a פוחח, and a סומא may and may not do. The גמרא asks why the מפטיר leads. רב פפא says it is for honor, and רבה בר שימי says it is to prevent quarrels. The case of a child מפטיר is answered with the honor of his father and teacher.

steps.title: Reading three verses at a time to the translator in the Prophets
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that in נביא the reader may give the מתורגמן three verses at a time. If each verse is a separate paragraph, he gives them one at a time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in the Prophets, the reader may read three verses to the translator at a time. If those three verses are three separate paragraphs, he reads them one by one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its rule about reading to the מתורגמן. In the Torah it is one verse at a time, but in נביא it can be three verses at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah gets stricter treatment because a mistaken translation of the Torah could lead people to an error in practical הלכה. נביא does not carry that risk, so the reader may give more at once. Still, if each verse is its own separate paragraph, they are treated as separate units and read one by one.

keyTerms.meaning: The Prophets (here, the הפטרה reading)
The translator who translated the reading into Aramaic for the congregation
A paragraph / paragraphs: a section marked off by a break in the text
One by one

phrases.english: And in the Prophets, three [verses at a time].
phrases.notes: Contrasts with the Torah, mentioned just before this, where only one verse at a time is read to the translator.

phrases.english: If the three of them were three separate paragraphs,
they read them one by one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's rule (on the previous amud) that only one Torah verse is read to the translator at a time.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In נביא, three verses at a time may be read to the translator, unless they are three separate paragraphs, in which case they are read one by one.

steps.title: Skipping is allowed in the Prophets but not in the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The משנה permits skipping from place to place in נביא but not in the Torah. The skip may be only as long as the time before the מתורגמן finishes translating.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may skip from place to place in the Prophets, but one may not skip in the Torah. How far may he skip? Only so far that the translator will not finish and have to stop and wait.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new rule: the reader may jump to a different spot in נביא, but not in the Torah. It also limits how big the jump can be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The limit is practical. While the translator is still translating the last verse, the reader rolls the scroll to the new spot. If the jump is so far that the translator finishes and the congregation has to sit and wait, that is disrespectful to the צבור, so it is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: They skip: jumping from one place in the text to another
Up to how much? How far?
He stops / finishes (here, the translator finishing his translation)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the הלכה that a הפטרה may combine passages from different places, while the Torah reading must stay in order.

phrases.english: One may skip in the Prophets
but one may not skip in the Torah.
And how far may he skip?
Only as far as the translator will not finish [and wait].
phrases.notes: The congregation must not be left waiting while the scroll is rolled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new rule in the same משנה, still contrasting Torah and נביא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Skipping is allowed in נביא but not in the Torah, and only as far as can be done before the translator finishes.
steps.whatToRemember: Throughout this משנה, the Torah is treated more strictly than נביא: one verse at a time to the translator, and no skipping.

steps.title: What do the three verses correspond to?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the three-verse minimum for each Torah reader is meant to correspond to.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: These three verses, what do they correspond to?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks a background question. It wants to know the reason behind the rule that each Torah reader reads at least three verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier part of the משנה taught that someone reading from the Torah may not read fewer than three verses. The גמרא assumes the number three is not random and asks what it represents.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
Corresponding to what? What does this represent?
Verses

steps.confusionAlert: "These three verses" does NOT refer to the three verses of נביא just mentioned. It refers to the earlier rule in the משנה that each person called to the Torah reads at least three verses.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
These three verses, what do they correspond to?
phrases.notes: He's asking about the minimum of three verses for each Torah reader.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to an earlier rule of the משנה, the three-verse minimum per reader.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the number three in the minimum Torah reading represents.

steps.title: רב אסי: corresponding to תורה, נביאים, and כתובים
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי answers that the three verses correspond to the three parts of תנ"ך: תורה, נביאים, and כתובים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: They correspond to the Torah, the Prophets, and the Writings.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי answers the question from the previous step. The three verses stand for the three sections of the Bible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each reader's three verses are a small reminder of the whole of תנ"ך, all three of its parts. This gives the number three a meaningful source rather than an arbitrary one.

keyTerms.meaning: Torah, Prophets, and Writings: the three parts of תנ"ך

phrases.english: Rav Asi said:
Corresponding to the Torah, the Prophets, and the Writings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי כְּנֶגֶד תּוֹרָה נְבִיאִים וּכְתוּבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The three verses correspond to תורה, נביאים, and כתובים.
steps.whatToRemember: Each Torah reader reads at least three verses, matching the three parts of תנ"ך (רב אסי).

steps.title: The גמרא repeats the translator rule from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule again: one verse to the translator in the Torah, three in נביא, and one by one if they are three separate paragraphs.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he should not read more than one verse to the translator. In the Prophets, three verses. And if the three of them are three separate paragraphs, he reads them one by one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next part of the משנה and quotes it again. This is a setup step: it repeats the rule so it can give a concrete example in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to the law here. The גמרא repeats the text on purpose, because the next line explains what "three verses that are three separate paragraphs" looks like in a real passage.

keyTerms.meaning: He should not read
More than one verse

phrases.english: And he should not read to the translator
more than one verse [at a time in the Torah],
and in the Prophets, three verses;
and if the three of them are three separate paragraphs,
he reads them one by one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא יִקְרָא לַמְּתוּרְגְּמָן יוֹתֵר מִפָּסוּק אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא leaves רב אסי's point and returns to the משנה's translator rule from step 1, quoting it again to explain it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah: one verse at a time to the translator. נביא: three, unless they are three separate paragraphs.

steps.title: An example of three verses that are three separate paragraphs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives an example from ישעיה 52:3-5: three verses in a row, each its own paragraph, which must be read to the translator one by one.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example: "For thus says the Lord: You were sold for nothing"; "For thus says the Lord God: My people went down at first to Egypt"; "And now, what do I have here, says the Lord."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the setup from the previous step by giving a real example of three neighboring verses that are each a separate paragraph.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These three verses in ישעיה stand right next to each other, yet each one is set off as its own paragraph. That makes them exactly the case the משנה described, so even in נביא the reader must give them to the translator one at a time.

keyTerms.meaning: For example
You were sold for nothing (ישעיה 52:3)
At first

phrases.english: For example: "For thus says the Lord:
You were sold for nothing" (Isaiah 52:3);
"For thus says the Lord God:
My people went down at first to Egypt" (Isaiah 52:4);
"And now, what do I have here, says the Lord" (Isaiah 52:5).
phrases.notes: This is one of three verses in a row, and each one is its own paragraph.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּגוֹן כִּי כֹה אָמַר ה׳ חִנָּם נִמְכַּרְתֶּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes step 5 by giving a concrete example of its rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ישעיה 52:3-5 are three separate paragraphs, so they are read to the translator one by one.
steps.whatToRemember: Even in נביא, where three verses may be given to the translator at once, verses that are each their own paragraph are read one by one. ישעיה 52:3-5 is the model case.

steps.title: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule on skipping
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings up the משנה's line again: skipping is allowed in נביא but not in the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: We may skip in the Prophets, but we may not skip in the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the משנה's rule about skipping so it can examine it. This is a setup line that prepares the challenge coming next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule makes a sharp contrast. Skipping from one place to another is allowed when reading נביא and forbidden when reading the Torah. The גמרא is about to test whether the Torah ban is really total.

keyTerms.meaning: We skip, meaning we jump from one passage to another during the reading
The Prophets, here meaning the הפטרה reading

phrases.english: We may skip in the Prophets
but we may not skip in the Torah.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Could be seen as the opening half of the קשיא in the next step
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the verse-by-verse translation rules to the next clause of the משנה, the rule about skipping.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Skipping is allowed in נביא and forbidden in the Torah.

steps.title: Contradiction from the כהן גדול's יום כיפור reading
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in יומא says the כהן גדול reads 'אחרי מות' and then 'אך בעשור', which is a skip in the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they contradicted it from another source: the כהן גדול reads 'אחרי מות' and then 'אך בעשור'. But he is skipping!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה with another משנה. On יום כיפור the כהן גדול jumps from one Torah passage to another, so skipping in the Torah seems to be allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אחרי מות' is in ויקרא chapter 16, and 'אך בעשור' is later, in chapter 23. Reading one and then the other means jumping over chapters of the Torah. That clashes with the rule that one may not skip in the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: And they contradicted it, meaning a source is brought that seems to clash with what we just learned
The יום כיפור service passage in ויקרא 16
The יום כיפור passage in ויקרא 23

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the כהן גדול is reading נביא here. Both passages are in the Torah, in ויקרא, which is exactly why this is a problem.

phrases.english: And they contradicted it: he reads 'After the death'
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה in יומא 68b about the כהן גדול on יום כיפור

phrases.english: and 'Only on the tenth day'
But he is skipping!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the Torah half of the rule quoted in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that one may not skip in the Torah
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The כהן גדול skips from ויקרא 16 to ויקרא 23 on יום כיפור, so skipping in the Torah must be allowed at least sometimes.

steps.title: אביי's first answer: it depends on how long the skip takes
steps.stepSummary: אביי says a short skip, finished before the מתורגמן stops translating, is allowed. A long skip is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is not difficult. Here, it is a case where the translator would finish and stop. There, it is a case where the translator would not finish.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction by splitting the cases according to how long the skip takes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If rolling the scroll to the new place takes so long that the מתורגמן finishes and the congregation waits in silence, skipping is forbidden. That is the משנה's case. If the reader gets there before the מתורגמן finishes, skipping is fine, as with the כהן גדול. On this view, the Torah ban covers only long skips.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult, the standard opening of an answer
Here... and there, used to split two sources into two different cases
That the translator will stop, meaning he finishes translating and has to wait

phrases.english: Abaye said: This is not difficult:
here, it is a case where the translator would stop,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה that forbids skipping in the Torah

phrases.english: and there, it is a case where the translator would not stop.
phrases.notes: This is the כהן גדול on יום כיפור, a short skip

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by the length of the skip
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that the Torah forbids every skip, which clashes with the כהן גדול's reading.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah forbids only a skip long enough that the מתורגמן stops. A short skip is allowed.

steps.title: The משנה's time limit was given only for Prophets
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects אביי's answer. The משנה gives the 'translator not stopping' limit only for נביא, which implies that in the Torah no skip is allowed at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught right on this topic: We may skip in the Prophets but not in the Torah. And how far may he skip? Only as far as the translator does not stop. This implies that in the Torah, there is no skipping at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's first answer using the wording of our own משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses the 'translator does not stop' limit to describe the allowed skip in נביא. If a short skip were also allowed in the Torah, the משנה would not contrast the Torah with נביא. So the Torah must have no skip at all, and אביי's distinction falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught right on this topic, introducing a challenge from the same source
By implication, meaning something we infer from what the text says
Not at all, not even a little

phrases.english: But it was taught right on this topic:
We may skip in the Prophets but we may not skip in the Torah,
and how far may he skip?
As far as the translator will not stop.
This implies that in the Torah
there is no skipping at all!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's first answer from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that a short skip is allowed in the Torah
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה gives the time limit only for נביא and contrasts it with the Torah. That implies the Torah allows no skip of any length.

steps.title: אביי's second answer: one topic versus two topics
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives a new answer. In the Torah you may skip within one topic but not between two different topics.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: This is not difficult. Here, it is one topic. There, it is two topics.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי drops his first answer and splits the cases in a new way, by subject matter instead of by time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול's two passages are both about יום כיפור, so they count as one topic, and skipping between them is allowed. The משנה's ban on skipping in the Torah refers to jumping between two different topics.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, signals that the earlier answer is dropped and a new one is given
One topic, meaning two passages about the same subject
Two topics, meaning passages about different subjects

steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the הלכה: skipping in the Torah is allowed only within the same subject.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said: This is not difficult:
here, it is one topic,
phrases.notes: The כהן גדול: both passages are about יום כיפור

phrases.english: there, it is two topics.
phrases.notes: The משנה's ban on skipping in the Torah

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer rejected in step 10 with a new distinction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by subject matter
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the time-based answer failed, the Torah seemed to forbid every skip.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the Torah, skipping is allowed within one topic, as with the כהן גדול, and forbidden between two topics.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the one-topic answer
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says this outright. In the Torah one may skip within one topic, in נביא even between two topics, and in both only if the מתורגמן does not stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so it was taught in a ברייתא: We may skip in the Torah within one topic, and in the Prophets even between two topics. In both cases, only if the translator will not stop.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that states אביי's second answer word for word, which supports it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא confirms the one-topic rule for the Torah and allows more freedom in נביא. It adds that the time limit applies to both. So even inside one topic, a Torah skip must be short enough that the מתורגמן does not finish and wait.
steps.whatToRemember: Final rule: In the Torah you may skip only within the same topic. In נביא you may skip even to a different topic. In both, the skip must be short enough that the מתורגמן does not stop and wait.
steps.confusionAlert: The time limit from אביי's first answer is not thrown out completely. It still applies, now on top of the one-topic rule, to both the Torah and נביא.

phrases.english: And so it was taught: We may skip in the Torah within one topic,
and in the Prophets even between two topics.

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן וְכָאן, בִּכְדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִפְסוֹק הַתּוּרְגְּמָן.
phrases.english: Both here and there, only if the translator will not stop.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's second answer from step 11.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's distinction between one topic and two topics
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that states the one-topic rule for the Torah and the two-topic rule for נביא, with the time limit applying to both
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Skipping is allowed in the Torah within one topic and in נביא even across topics. In both cases the skip must be short enough that the מתורגמן does not stop.

steps.title: Another teaching on skipping between books of the Prophets
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא teaches that you may not skip from one book of נביא to another. Within תרי עשר (the Twelve Prophets) you may skip, but only going forward.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: One may not skip from one prophet's book to another prophet's book. But within the Twelve Prophets, one may skip, as long as he does not skip backward, from the end of the book to its beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more ברייתא to finish the topic of skipping. This one sets a limit on skipping in נביא: you may skip within a book, but not from one book to a different book.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said that in נביא you may even skip between two topics. This ברייתא adds a limit: that only applies inside one book, not from one book of נביא to another. The twelve small prophets are counted as one book, so skipping among them is allowed, but only forward and never backward.

keyTerms.meaning: They skip (jump from one place in the text to another)
The Twelve Prophets (תרי עשר), counted as one book
From the end of the book back to its beginning, meaning skipping backward

steps.whatToRemember: Summary of the skipping rules: in the Torah you may skip only within one topic. In נביא you may skip even between topics, but only within one book. תרי עשר counts as one book, and there you may skip only forward. In every case, the skip must be finished before the מתורגמן stops.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 12. That step allowed skipping between topics in נביא. This step is about something else: skipping between separate books of נביא, which is not allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the practical rules for how a הפטרה may be put together from different places.

phrases.english: It is taught in another baraita:
One may not skip from prophet to prophet,
phrases.notes: Meaning from one book of Prophets to a different book.

phrases.english: but within the prophets of the Twelve, he may skip,
phrases.notes: The twelve short prophets are written together as one book.

phrases.english: provided that he does not skip
from the end of the book to its beginning.
phrases.notes: In other words, no skipping backward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further limit to the rules about skipping from the ברייתא in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No skipping between separate books of נביא. Within תרי עשר, skipping is allowed only forward.

steps.title: The הפטרה reader leads the other parts of the service
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that the מפטיר also gets the honor of leading פורס על שמע, leading the עמידה, and, if he is a כהן, doing ברכת כהנים. If he is a child, his father or teacher leads in his place.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The one who reads the הפטרה is the one who leads the blessings before שמע, goes before the ark to lead the prayer, and lifts his hands for ברכת כהנים. If he is a child, his father or his teacher goes before the ark in his place.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says the person who reads the הפטרה is also given the other leading honors in the service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מפטיר is given these extra honors along with reading the הפטרה. The משנה also handles a problem: a child may read the הפטרה but cannot lead the prayers. So his father or teacher takes those honors instead of him.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)
The one who concludes with a reading from the Prophets (the הפטרה reader)
Leads the opening part of קריאת שמע for the congregation (קדיש, ברכו, and the first ברכה)
Goes before the ark, meaning he leads the עמידה as חזן
Lifts his hands, meaning he says ברכת כהנים (only if he is a כהן)
Lead in his place, on his behalf

steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא will soon ask why the מפטיר is given these honors. This is the basis of the custom of honoring the מפטיר.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The one who concludes with a reading from the Prophets,
he is the one who leads the blessing before Shema,
and he passes before the ark,
phrases.notes: He leads the עמידה.

phrases.english: and he lifts his hands.
phrases.notes: Only if he is a כהן.

phrases.english: And if he was a minor,

phrases.aramaic: אָבִיו אוֹ רַבּוֹ עוֹבְרִין עַל יָדוֹ.
phrases.english: his father or his teacher passes before the ark in his place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic: who receives which honors in the service.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מפטיר leads פורס על שמע and the עמידה and does נשיאת כפים. If he is a קטן, his father or teacher leads in his place.

steps.title: What a child may and may not do in בית הכנסת
steps.stepSummary: A קטן may read from the Torah and translate it. He may not lead פורס על שמע, lead the עמידה, or do ברכת כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A child may read from the Torah and translate it. But he may not lead the blessing before שמע, may not go before the ark to lead the prayer, and may not lift his hands for ברכת כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a list. It tells us which jobs a child is allowed to do in בית הכנסת and which he is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading and translating the Torah are things a child is allowed to do. Leading the congregation in prayer and blessing them are different: a child cannot lead the adults in their prayers or blessing. This explains the previous step, where the father or teacher leads in place of a child מפטיר.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor (a boy under בר מצוה)
Reads from the Torah in public
Translates the reading into Aramaic for the congregation

steps.confusionAlert: A beginner might think a child cannot be called to the Torah at all. This משנה clearly says he may read from the Torah. He only may not lead the prayers or the blessing.

phrases.english: A minor may read from the Torah and translate.
But he may not lead the blessing before Shema,
and he may not pass before the ark,
and he may not lift his hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה and explains the limits on a קטן mentioned in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קטן may read the Torah and translate it, but may not lead פורס על שמע, lead the עמידה, or do נשיאת כפים.

steps.title: What a person with exposed limbs may and may not do
steps.stepSummary: A פוחח may lead פורס את שמע and may translate. He may not read from the Torah, lead the עמידה, or do ברכת כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person whose limbs are exposed may lead the blessing before שמע and may translate. But he may not read from the Torah, may not go before the ark to lead the prayer, and may not lift his hands for ברכת כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the case of a פוחח, a person whose clothes are torn so parts of his body show. It lists what he may do and what he may not do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list for a פוחח is different from the list for a קטן. A פוחח may not read from the Torah, out of respect for the Torah. He also may not stand in front to lead the עמידה or bless the people, out of respect for the congregation. Translating and leading פורס על שמע are allowed for him.

keyTerms.meaning: A person dressed in torn clothes, so that his limbs are uncovered
Leads the opening of שמע (same honor as פורס על שמע, slightly different wording)
He may not read from the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: So far this משנה has given three lists. The מפטיר gets all the leading honors. A קטן may read and translate, but may not lead. A פוחח may lead פורס על שמע and translate, but may not read the Torah, lead the עמידה, or bless the people. The next step adds the סומא.
steps.confusionAlert: Notice the reverse pattern. A קטן may read the Torah but may not lead פורס על שמע. A פוחח may lead פורס על שמע but may not read the Torah. The reasons are different: the child's problem is his age, while the פוחח's problem is respect for the Torah and the congregation.

phrases.english: One whose limbs are exposed may lead the blessing before Shema and may translate.
But he may not read from the Torah,
and he may not pass before the ark,
and he may not lift his hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list in the משנה with another type of person who has a different set of limits.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פוחח may lead פורס על שמע and translate, but may not read the Torah, lead the עמידה, or do נשיאת כפים.

steps.title: A blind person may lead the שמע blessings and translate
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a סומא may lead פורס על שמע and may translate. רבי יהודה says that someone who has never seen the luminaries may not lead פורס על שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: A blind person may lead פורס את שמע and may translate the Torah reading. רבי יהודה says: anyone who has never seen the sun, moon and stars in his whole life may not lead פורס על שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more case to its list of people who may or may not lead parts of the service. This case is a blind person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא allows a סומא to lead the blessings before שמע, even though the first blessing praises God for creating the lights (יוצר המאורות). רבי יהודה limits this. Someone blind from birth has never benefited from seeing light, so he cannot say that blessing. Someone who became blind later did once see the lights, so he may lead.

keyTerms.meaning: A blind person
The luminaries: the sun, moon and stars
In all his days, meaning ever in his life

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה does not forbid every blind person. He only forbids someone who never saw light in his whole life, meaning a person blind from birth. Someone who became blind later may still lead.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the idea that saying a blessing about something may depend on having personally benefited from it.

phrases.english: A blind person may lead the blessings of Shema and may translate.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Anyone who has never seen the luminaries in his life,
phrases.notes: This means someone blind from birth.

phrases.english: may not lead the blessings of Shema.
phrases.notes: The first blessing praises God for creating the lights.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of who may lead parts of the service, adding the case of a blind person after the קטן and the פוחח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סומא may lead פורס על שמע and may translate. According to רבי יהודה, someone blind from birth may not lead פורס על שמע.

steps.title: Why does the הפטרה reader get to lead the prayers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking the reason for the משנה's rule that the מפטיר also leads פורס על שמע, the עמידה, and ברכת כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion by asking for the reason behind a rule in the משנה. This question sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (step 14) said the מפטיר gets extra honors: leading פורס על שמע, leading the עמידה, and doing ברכת כהנים if he is a כהן. It never explained why. The גמרא now asks for that reason.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
What is the reason?
The person who reads the הפטרה from נביא

steps.confusionAlert: The question 'מאי טעמא' is NOT about the blind person just mentioned. It goes back to the earlier rule in the משנה that the מפטיר leads the prayers.

phrases.english: Gemara: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: Meaning the reason the הפטרה reader is given these other roles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה rule from step 14 and asks for its reasoning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the מפטיר receive the honor of leading פורס על שמע, the עמידה, and ברכת כהנים?

steps.title: First answer: to give him honor
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the מפטיר gets these roles out of respect for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: it is because of honor.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the first answer to the question. The מפטיר is given these roles to honor him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a child may read the הפטרה, so being called for it could feel less important than being called to the Torah. To make up for this, the community gives the מפטיר the more honored jobs of leading the prayers.

keyTerms.meaning: Honor, respect

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Because of honor.
phrases.notes: Reading the הפטרה, which even a child may do, could seem like a lesser role, so he is honored in other ways.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מפטיר leads the prayers so that he receives honor.

steps.title: Second answer: to prevent quarrels
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שימי says the reason is to stop the מפטיר from fighting with whoever else would lead the prayers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר שימי said: it is because otherwise they would come to quarrel.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different reason for the same rule. The goal is to prevent a fight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose someone else were chosen to lead the prayers. The מפטיר, who is already standing up front, might argue with that person over who should lead. Giving the job to the מפטיר from the start avoids the argument.

keyTerms.meaning: To quarrel, to fight

phrases.english: Rabba bar Shimi said:
Because they will come to quarrel.
phrases.notes: The הפטרה reader might fight with whoever else is chosen to lead.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר שִׁימִי אָמַר: מִשּׁוּם דְּאָתֵי לְאִינְּצוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reason from רב פפא's reason in step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מפטיר leads the prayers so that no quarrel breaks out.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between the two reasons?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in which case the two reasons would lead to different results.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two reasons ever lead to a different practical outcome. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons lead to the same rule in a normal case. So the גמרא looks for a situation where one reason applies and the other does not.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two answers given in steps 19 and 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what case does it matter whether the reason is honor or preventing a quarrel?

steps.title: The difference: when the prayer leader serves for free
steps.stepSummary: The two reasons differ when the one leading the prayers is not paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them where he does it for free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two reasons give different results when leading the prayers is unpaid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the prayer leader serves for free, there is nothing to gain from the job, so people are unlikely to fight over it. On רבה בר שימי's reason, the מפטיר would then not need to be given the role. On רב פפא's reason, the מפטיר still deserves the honor, so he should still lead.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
For free, without pay

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
where he does it for free.
phrases.notes: With no pay involved, people are unlikely to fight, but giving honor is still relevant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When the prayer leader is unpaid, the quarrel reason no longer applies but the honor reason still does.

steps.title: Challenge from the case of a child reader
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבה בר שימי. The משנה says that when the מפטיר is a child, his father or teacher leads in his place. But a child would not quarrel.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: if the מפטיר is a child, his father or teacher leads in his place. If you say the reason is to prevent quarrels, would a child really get into a quarrel?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses a line from the משנה to attack רבה בר שימי's reason. Steps 24 and 25 respond to this challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קטן is not allowed to lead the prayers at all (step 15), so he has no claim to fight over. Even so, the משנה says his father or teacher leads instead of him. The challenger assumes this case does not fit the idea of preventing a quarrel.

keyTerms.meaning: Lead the prayers in his place
If you say
Someone who would get into a quarrel

steps.whyThisMatters: The question sets up the next move. Either רבה בר שימי will be defended, or רב פפא's reason of honor will be shown to fit the משנה better.

phrases.english: We learned: And if he was a minor,

phrases.aramaic: אָבִיו אוֹ רַבּוֹ עוֹבְרִין עַל יָדוֹ.
phrases.english: his father or his teacher leads in his place.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה from step 14.

phrases.english: If you say it is because of quarreling,
is a minor someone who quarrels?
phrases.notes: A child has no claim to lead, so there is nothing to fight over.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: וְאִם הָיָה קָטָן — אָבִיו אוֹ רַבּוֹ עוֹבְרִין עַל יָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה to challenge the reason given by רבה בר שימי in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר שימי's reason that the מפטיר leads the prayers in order to prevent quarrels.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A child cannot lead the prayers, so he has no reason to fight. Yet the משנה still gives the role to his father or teacher. So preventing a quarrel cannot be the reason behind the rule.

steps.title: The same problem hits the honor reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. If the child case is a problem for רבה בר שימי, it is just as much a problem for רב פפא, because a child has no honor that needs protecting.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what would you say instead, that the reason is honor? Does a child have honor?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is defending רבה בר שימי by showing that the other opinion, רב פפא's 'honor' reason, has the exact same difficulty with the child case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 argued that a child would not fight, so the 'quarrel' reason fails. Here the גמרא answers that the 'honor' reason fails just as badly, since a child is not someone whose honor matters. Since both reasons face the same question, the child case cannot be used to knock out רבה בר שימי alone.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But what then?' A phrase that turns a challenge back on the other side
A minor (a child)
Someone who has honor that must be respected

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא rejecting רב פפא. It is a 'you have the same problem' move, meant to protect רבה בר שימי from the challenge in step 23.

phrases.english: Rather, what? Is it because of honor?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking about the other option, which is רב פפא's reason.

phrases.english: Is a child someone who has honor?!
phrases.notes: The answer is obviously no: a child doesn't have that kind of honor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23's challenge by turning the same difficulty against רב פפא's reason
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's explanation that the מפטיר leads out of respect for him (step 19)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה also gives the child case for רב פפא, yet a child has no honor to protect. So the child case proves nothing against רבה בר שימי specifically.

steps.title: The honor belongs to the father and teacher
steps.stepSummary: For רב פפא, the answer is that when a child is מפטיר, the honor at stake belongs to his father and his teacher.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, there is the honor of his father and the honor of his teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רב פפא handles the child case: the father or teacher leads because the honor is theirs. This sets up the next move, a similar answer for רבה בר שימי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The honor does not belong to the child himself. It moves to the adults connected to him, his father and his teacher, which is why the משנה has them lead in his place. By the same pattern, רבה בר שימי can say that the quarrel to avoid is one with the father or teacher.

keyTerms.meaning: There is / there exists
The honor of his father
The honor of his teacher

steps.whyThisMatters: It explains the משנה's wording, that the child's father or teacher leads in his place. It also gives a model that lets both reasons survive the child case.

phrases.english: Rather, there is the honor of his father
and the honor of his teacher,
phrases.notes: The גמרא isn't done here: next it applies the same logic to רבה בר שימי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִיכָּא כְּבוֹד אָבִיו וּכְבוֹד רַבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the counter-difficulty raised against רב פפא in step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shifting the relevant party: the honor belongs to the child's father and teacher, not the child
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A child has no honor, so the honor reason seems not to apply to a child מפטיר
steps.terutzMaskana: The honor of the child's father and teacher is involved, so they lead in his place. This prepares a parallel answer for רבה בר שימי.
